domains.label: Mathematics & optimization
domains.description: Mathematical constructions, inequalities, generic optimizers and numerical algorithms.
domains.why_it_matters: Candidate objects or algorithms can improve explicit bounds, feasibility, approximation error or search efficiency.

domains.label: Operations research
domains.description: Routing, packing, scheduling, allocation and constraint models with an operational objective.
domains.why_it_matters: These tasks study how to use limited space, time and resources under explicit constraints.

domains.label: Machine learning & language
domains.description: Learning algorithms, generic prediction, language benchmarks, retrieval and digital-agent behavior.
domains.why_it_matters: Compare generalization, reasoning, learning procedures and retrieval quality across defined data and benchmark tasks.

domains.label: Software engineering
domains.description: Program synthesis, code repair, repository tasks and verification workflows.
domains.why_it_matters: Correctness and task completion expose whether generated software satisfies a program or repository contract.

domains.label: Computer systems & hardware
domains.description: Kernels, compilers, databases, datacenters, circuits and infrastructure optimization.
domains.why_it_matters: Latency, throughput, resource use and hardware constraints connect candidate programs to computing efficiency.

domains.label: Robotics & control
domains.description: Feedback controllers, embodied policies and rewards for locomotion or manipulation.
domains.why_it_matters: Closed-loop behavior tests stability, task completion and control performance, often in simulation.

domains.label: Physics
domains.description: Physical models, cosmology, quantum systems, transport, event reconstruction and physical-law inference.
domains.why_it_matters: Compare physical constructions, inferred relationships and numerical methods against declared measurements or simulations.

domains.label: Chemistry & materials
domains.description: Reaction kinetics, chemical transformations, material properties and constitutive models.
domains.why_it_matters: Infer stress–strain relationships, integrate chemical reaction dynamics and predict reaction outcomes or material properties.

domains.label: Biology & health
domains.description: Growth, biological sequences, cellular or neural data and biological or medical prediction targets.
domains.why_it_matters: Fit growth and population models, analyze RNA and cellular data, and learn predictive relationships in biological imagery and neural activity.

domains.label: Earth & environment
domains.description: Earth-system and environmental models, observations, prediction and resource-control targets.
domains.why_it_matters: Modeling environmental observations can test forecasting or process prediction under a defined dataset protocol.

domains.label: Finance & economics
domains.description: Economic decisions, allocation, mechanism design, structural models and financial policies.
domains.why_it_matters: Study economic models and decision rules under explicit objectives, information limits and feasibility constraints.

domains.label: Mixed / unclassified
domains.description: The available metadata describes a mixed suite or does not identify one primary application domain.
domains.why_it_matters: Keep mixed or underspecified packages visible while more detailed target and evaluation evidence is recorded.

task_types.label: Mathematical construction
task_types.description: Construct a discrete or continuous object under mathematical constraints.
task_types.why_it_matters: Feasibility and an explicit extremal objective make candidate configurations directly comparable.

task_types.label: Combinatorial optimization
task_types.description: Design a constructive heuristic or search strategy for a discrete allocation problem.
task_types.why_it_matters: Solution quality and feasibility measure how a method navigates a constrained search space.

task_types.label: Black-box optimization
task_types.description: Design an optimizer, acquisition function or selection policy for an objective oracle.
task_types.why_it_matters: Evaluation budgets and attained objective values test search efficiency rather than one fixed solution.

task_types.label: Symbolic regression
task_types.description: Recover an equation, scaling law or symbolic-regression procedure from data.
task_types.why_it_matters: Held-out error tests whether a compact functional expression predicts beyond the fitted examples.

task_types.label: Numerical solver
task_types.description: Integrate or simulate specified dynamics, solve equations, or design numerical integration and sampling procedures.
task_types.why_it_matters: Accuracy and numerical cost quantify behavior on specified functions, states or trajectories.

task_types.label: Prediction & model design
task_types.description: Fit, infer, train or design a predictive or generative model, representation or parameter estimate.
task_types.why_it_matters: Prediction error or task return evaluates learned behavior on the declared data or environment.

task_types.label: Hyperparameter search
task_types.description: Optimize training settings or model hyperparameters.
task_types.why_it_matters: A held-out objective tests the quality and cost of selecting a model configuration.

task_types.label: Language & reasoning
task_types.description: Optimize prompts, scaffolds or outputs on language, reasoning or grid-inference benchmarks.
task_types.why_it_matters: Measure compositional reasoning, language understanding and constraint satisfaction on specified benchmark cases.

task_types.label: Agent workflow
task_types.description: Design an agent workflow for tools, web environments, planning or digital tasks.
task_types.why_it_matters: End-to-end task completion tests how actions and tools are coordinated across a trajectory.

task_types.label: Software generation & repair
task_types.description: Generate, repair, review or verify program code.
task_types.why_it_matters: Executable tests or repository task outcomes connect a proposed change to software behavior.

task_types.label: Systems optimization
task_types.description: Improve kernel, compiler, infrastructure, hardware or program-performance decisions.
task_types.why_it_matters: Correctness plus cost or performance measurements test whether systems changes are useful.

task_types.label: Control policy
task_types.description: Design a feedback controller, sequential decision rule or embodied action policy.
task_types.why_it_matters: Sequential outcomes test decisions under changing state and information constraints.

task_types.label: Reward design
task_types.description: Design a reward for a learning controller or policy.
task_types.why_it_matters: The resulting trained behavior tests whether the reward induces the intended task behavior.

task_types.label: Information retrieval
task_types.why_it_matters: Relevance measurements compare ranking functions and document-search quality across different collections.

task_types.label: Constraint modeling
task_types.description: Reformulate or solve explicit satisfiability, logic or mathematical-program constraints.
task_types.why_it_matters: Feasibility and solver efficiency expose the value of the model formulation or solver policy.

task_types.label: Benchmark generation
task_types.description: Generate benchmark functions or embodied evaluation tasks.
task_types.why_it_matters: Produce controlled instances for probing evaluation coverage, difficulty and optimizer or policy robustness.

task_types.label: Signal processing
task_types.description: Filter or transform a signal under error, noise and smoothness criteria.
task_types.why_it_matters: Output fidelity and robustness test whether useful signal structure survives processing.

task_types.label: Unclassified task type
task_types.description: The catalog does not yet specify a clear candidate or evaluation operation.
task_types.why_it_matters: Expose gaps in the recorded optimization contract so future catalog curation can resolve them.

Available metadata is an opaque or broad suite/task label, insufficient to establish one scientific domain and candidate operation.

methodology.classification_authority: Arena editorial inference from the pinned catalog; these labels are not a taxonomy supplied or certified by the source authors.
methodology.unit: One canonical registered task package (task ID). This snapshot merges 253 upstream aliases; remaining parameter variants and distinct protocols are separate packages. Counts are not counts of unique scientific problems.
methodology.primary_domain: Exactly one primary application domain per package. Classification follows the candidate objective/target, not paper-title keywords or the subject of QA/retrieval documents. Cross-domain connections are discussed in definitions, never counted twice.
methodology.task_type: Exactly one task type per package, describing the candidate operation independently of application domain.
methodology.rules: Ordered first-match rules: explicit scientific targets and mixed-family exceptions, reviewed task groups, defaults for each of 357 source families, then unknown. Conditions within a rule are AND; values within one condition are OR. Historical rule IDs containing unsupported do not override current catalog availability.
methodology.evidence: Annotations retain the matched rule, rationale, task name, description, metric, source family and paper IDs. Exact-ID lists were resolved using catalog/duplicates.json at source commit 5729caa7a3bd4e66c39a447c0d4ee56dc8fa0935; merged predecessors had consistent domain/type assignments. New family classifications review catalog/tasks.json, labels.area, candidate interfaces and catalog/science/*.json at that commit. Tasks imported later from source commit a5e50ed6355b14e0a09e98a1afeba8e4e4c9b1fd (the prize-bank collections and the MCTS-AHD admissible-set task restored after an incorrect duplicate merge) were classified from catalog/science/prize*.json, labels.area and their candidate contracts at that commit. These are editorial classifications, not endorsements of upstream scientific-importance or open-problem labels.
methodology.percentages: Each domain distribution and each task-type distribution uses all catalog packages as denominator. Largest-remainder rounding to 0.1 percentage point makes each partition sum to 100.0%; ties use taxonomy definition order.
methodology.availability: Executable and unsupported counts preserve source protocol status. Classification neither installs an environment nor establishes runtime readiness, fidelity, reproducibility or Arena conformance.
methodology.papers: Corpus paper counts exclude the 25 supplemental source IDs declared in non_paper_source_ids: SCiEL, Santa 2025 and 23 science collections. This snapshot covers 98 corpus paper IDs and 123 source groups. unique_paper_count is a compatibility alias for source_group_count; label it source groups. Per-group paper_count counts corpus IDs, not independently verified publications. Per-group source_group_count includes supplements; group coverage overlaps.
methodology.families: Family counts exclude null source families. Families can span domains/types and must not be summed across groups.
methodology.coverage: Coverage rows are overlapping indicators, each using the complete package denominator. They are not a distribution and their percentages must not be summed.
methodology.scientific_relevance: why_it_matters describes the modeled function or evaluation operation, not a subjective scientific-importance ranking or a claim that the benchmark produced a discovery.
methodology.refresh: Changing catalog or taxonomy requires rebuilding insights.json. Offline validation compares digests, every assignment and all aggregate totals before serving the Python API.
